findings.source_quote: ταῦτα δὲ ἔλεγεν εἰδὼς ὅτι μετὰ τοῦ προσκυνῆσαι καὶ τὴν κατ’ αὐτοῦ εἶχεν ἐξουσίαν καὶ οὕτως τῆς μελλούσης δόξης καὶ βασιλείας ἑαυτὸν ἀφῄρει
findings.english_quote: He said this knowing that, with that act of worship, he would also gain authority over him, and so the latter would deprive himself of the glory and kingdom to come.
findings.issue: The draft explicitly switches the subject from the temporary king to the future king at “the latter would deprive himself.” This is a defensible contextual interpretation, but the Greek does not expressly introduce a new subject at ἀφῄρει. The notes explain the authority relationship and separately discuss κατενεχύραζεν, but do not disclose this subject switch or the grammatical alternative of continuing the temporary king as subject. Who deprives himself of the future glory and kingdom is a material interpretive uncertainty.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a note specifically addressing ἑαυτὸν ἀφῄρει: explain that the main text supplies the future king as its subject because the threatened loss concerns his future glory and kingdom, while preserving the alternative that the unexpressed subject continues to be the temporary king. Distinguish this contextual interpretation from the supplied wording; no textual correction is required. Submit the updated passage and notes for fresh review.

findings.source_quote: καὶ τοὺς ἀγαθοὺς εἰς τὸ θεοῦ δεῖπνον εἰσάγειν ἐκ τῆς μεταμελείας
findings.english_quote: and to bring into God’s banquet those who have become good through a change of heart
findings.issue: The draft interprets ἐκ τῆς μεταμελείας as explaining how the people became good. That contextual attachment is defensible, but another material reading attaches the phrase to εἰσάγειν: their change of heart or regret supplies the grounds for bringing the good into the banquet. The lexical note discusses meanings of μεταμέλεια but presents its production of goodness as established rather than disclosing this attachment alternative.
findings.suggested_revision: Expand the note to preserve both relationships: “those who have become good through a change of heart” and “to bring the good into God’s banquet on account of their change of heart.” Explain why the main text selects the former. Alternatively, propose a more attachment-transparent rendering, such as “and to bring the good into God’s banquet as a result of their change of heart,” with a note explaining what the causal phrase may qualify. Any updated wording or notes require fresh review.
